articles.title: ‘Made us sit on lap’: Bihar girls accuse headmaster of entering washroom, harassing
articles.summary: Allegations of a headmaster's inappropriate actions have surfaced at a Nawada government school.  These incidents follow a Class X student's alleged molestation in Jamui.  Girls reported the headmaster entered their washroom and touched them inappropriately.  The headmaster was arrested under the POCSO Act after protests by students and parents.  These events highlight serious concerns regarding the safety of minor girls in Bihar.

articles.title: Union minister Giriraj inaugurates KFC, sparks debate over his jhatka meat remarks
articles.summary: Union minister Giriraj Singh recently graced the opening of a KFC outlet in Begusarai, stirring up a frenzy on social media. This event brought back his controversial remarks suggesting Hindus should choose only jhatka meat and steer clear of halal options. This reopening has reignited the debate surrounding his dietary suggestions and the implications for cultural dining.

articles.title: Intruder shoots teacher dead inside UP school, kills himself
articles.summary: A 26-year-old teacher was fatally shot inside a Lakhimpur Kheri school by a 28-year-old man. The attacker then shot himself, causing panic among hundreds of students present. Police are investigating how the assailant entered the school with a firearm. The victim's family alleged the man had been pressuring her to marry him. This incident follows a similar fatal attack on a teacher in Faridabad.

articles.title: Russia planning 'grey zone operations'? Why is Europe intuitively spooked
articles.summary: Much of what worries Western officials is not a tank invasion but something harder to pin down. Drones drifting into Baltic airspace, sabotage at airports, cyberattacks, plots involving criminal networks operating far from Russia's own territory. Individually, each incident can be denied or dismissed as an accident but likely form a pattern that lets Moscow probe Nato's resolve without technically starting a war.

articles.title: Fake Apple centre in Gurgaon ‘shortlisted’ elderly in US, scared them into paying up to $20k
articles.summary: A sham Apple service centre in Palam Vihar was busted by Gurgaon police.  Elderly US citizens were targeted with fake privacy and virus warnings.  Impersonators then demanded thousands of dollars using bogus Federal Trade Commission notices.  Police have traced transactions worth two crore rupees from fifteen victims.  Eleven individuals were arrested, and the main operator remains at large.

articles.title: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has ‘China advice’ for American AI companies
articles.summary: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has warned that competition with China must not become a reason for American technology companies to bypass critical safety standards and guardrails. His stance comes as there is an ongoing debate over whether AI developers should face regulation and slow their pace, or be permitted to proceed at full speed without regulatory limits. He said, "I don’t think we should use China as the bogeyman for not making progress on our own efforts on AI safety."

articles.title: Bihar molestation case: Main accused Nandan Yadav injured in police encounter
articles.summary: In a police operation targeting Nandan Yadav, the accused in a Jamui molestation case, he sustained a bullet injury to his leg and is now receiving medical treatment. This follow-up comes after viral videos of the incident sparked outrage across social media. Authorities have identified and charged several individuals related to the case, with investigations ongoing and steps being taken to erase the circulated videos.

articles.title: PM classmate’s battle for land continues despite BJP MLA's exit
articles.summary: Asgar Ali Vora struggles to regain his land after a developer relinquished possession.  He had purchased the property in 1989 and alleged developers took possession in 2011.  After meeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi, one developer relinquished the land.  However, another developer allegedly continues to retain possession of the property.  Police have registered a non-cognisable offence against the involved developers.

articles.title: First gold for India at Asian Games 2026: Women's cricket team beats SL in final
articles.summary: India secured their first gold medal at the Asian Games 2026. Harmanpreet Kaur's team defeated Sri Lanka in the women's cricket final. Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma provided a strong opening partnership. Richa Ghosh's quick cameo propelled India to a formidable total. This victory marked India's seventh medal overall in the competition.

articles.title: Father of dalit IIT-Bombay student, who died by suicide in 2023, detained at stir
articles.summary: Darshan Solanki's father was detained by Powai police on Monday. He was protesting caste discrimination on the IIT-B campus. The father sought a meeting with the IIT-B director to discuss suicide prevention steps. Protesters were denied entry, and one alleged police manhandling. This incident follows three student suicides at the institute this year.

articles.title: 1834 Nantucket home sold for $9.5m, now listed for $32 million
articles.summary: A historic Nantucket home built around 1834 for sea captain George C. Gardner is now for sale. This Greek Revival residence has undergone significant moves and two major restoration efforts. The 7,000-plus-square-foot house combines 19th-century character with modern amenities. It features a swimming pool and a separate three-bedroom guest cottage on the property. The property is situated on Nantucket’s Main Street, close to local attractions.

articles.title: Judge allows Texas land swap giving SpaceX over 700 refuge acres
Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu to engineers: Use AI but never cede
articles.summary: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu cautions engineers about excessive AI use in software creation. He advises using AI tools without losing essential understanding of the development process. An engineer described AI generating nearly all software components, causing team dissatisfaction. This rapid adoption of AI tools outpaces industry comprehension, inviting potential disaster. Engineers are working long hours directing AI, leading to a soul-sucking experience.

articles.title: Why children hide school marks from parents, according to psychology
articles.summary: Many children conceal their underwhelming academic performance due to the weight of parental expectations. Disheartening interactions with parents can push students towards disengagement strategies in coping with stress. Conversely, when parents offer support, it nurtures a willingness to tackle academic difficulties. If children believe their achievements determine parental approval, they may also experience heightened anxiety during tests. Grasping this relationship can enable parents to promote open dialogue about academic struggles.

articles.title: 3 pose as cops, gang-rape Delhi teen near Kalkaji Mandir
articles.summary: A 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped by three men posing as police officers. The incident occurred in a park near Kalkaji Mandir after the girl and her friend visited the temple. Police received a PCR call and reached the spot, taking the girl for medical examination. Authorities are scanning CCTV footage and gathering information to identify the accused.

articles.title: Shafali Verma creates history, surpasses Laura Wolvaardt for major T20I record
articles.summary: Shafali Verma has etched her name in history by breaking the record for the most T20I runs in a calendar year, surpassing Laura Wolvaardt's previous achievement. With an impressive tally that includes one century and seven fifties, Verma has showcased remarkable consistency this season. Alongside Smriti Mandhana, they have solidified their record partnership, totaling over 4,000 runs as Indian openers.

articles.title: Will shut Iranian flights from tomorrow: US new arm-twist move against Tehran
Gold jumps 60% to Rs 1.57L from Rs 98,000 a year ago; sales fall 15%, coins gain
articles.summary: In Mumbai's spot market on Monday, gold was trading at Rs 1.57 lakh per 10 grams, including 3% goods and services tax. This was around 60% higher than the Rs 98,000 per 10 grams recorded on Ganesh Chaturthi last year, which fell on August 28.

articles.title: India survive huge Japan scare, win by two runs in historic T20I
articles.summary: In a nail-biting finish, India clinched a historic T20 International victory against Japan by a narrow margin of just two runs. Although facing challenges from Japan's spin bowlers, India's own spinners made a remarkable comeback, ultimately securing the team's 200th win in men's T20 cricket. This match showcased the resilience and strategic prowess of both sides, making it a memorable encounter.

articles.title: India sees rise in both overweight and underweight
articles.summary: India's latest health survey shows below-normal BMI is not decreasing while overweight and obesity are rising. Women's normal BMI range fell significantly, and men's share also shrank considerably. Below-normal BMI increased in many states, and overweight or obesity rose even more widely. Urban areas show higher rates of both underweight and overweight conditions for men and women.

articles.title: India’s space sovereignty: From building missions to building depth
articles.summary: India has proven its capability to design and launch complex spacecraft independently.  The nation now focuses on building industrial depth for space sovereignty and self-reliance.  A burgeoning private sector and numerous startups are transforming India's space ecosystem.  Future missions aim for a space station and lunar exploration by 2040.  Component-level self-reliance remains a critical challenge for sustained space endeavors.

Is not singing Vande Mataram punishable offence? Supreme Court to examine
articles.summary: The Supreme Court will not decide on the National Song's stanza length now.  It will examine if not singing it can be a punishable offense.  The court referenced a past ruling stating no one can be punished for not singing the National Anthem.  The Centre opposed the challenge, citing a "naxalite mindset" for questioning the song.  The court asked the Centre to file its response to the public interest litigation.

articles.title: Space-age warfare: DRDO develops a more powerful laser that can take out drones at 5 km
articles.summary: India's DRDO seeks industry partners for its 30kW counter-drone laser weapon.  Final trials concluded in August 2025, demonstrating the technology's readiness.  This system targets drone swarms and surveillance sensors up to five kilometers.  Smaller laser systems are already in production and ordered by the military.  This initiative enhances India's layered air defence architecture against evolving threats.

articles.title: Padma Shri scholar spent 5 decades learning and teaching Hindi in Russia
articles.summary: Dr. Liudmila Khokhlova has been honored with the prestigious Padma Shri award for her remarkable contributions to the study of Indian languages. Over the span of more than fifty years, she has delved deep into languages such as Hindi and Punjabi. Her scholarly endeavors also include translating crucial Sikh scriptures into Russian. This prestigious award celebrates her significant impact on the field of Indological studies.

articles.title: Major milestone for energy exploration: ONGC strikes gas 43 km off Odisha coast

articles.title: Vansh Bedi reported fixing approach during DPL; DDCA seeks BCCI intervention

The Delhi and District Cricket Association is now looking to the BCCI for guidance following this incident linked to a sting operation conducted by a media outlet.

articles.title: Swept away by raging Teesta in Bengal, elephant calf saved by four fishermen
articles.summary: Five fishermen bravely rescued a newborn elephant calf from the Teesta river.  They spotted the calf struggling and pulled it onto their small row boat.  Forest personnel provided immediate veterinary care to the distressed young elephant.  Efforts were then made to reunite the calf with its mother.  After two hours, the calf was successfully reunited and seen nursing.

articles.title: Wife sold Rs 25 soft drink for Rs 26; husband faced case for 13 years, HC quashes it
articles.summary: The court has quashed the prosecution, which arose from an allegation that the man had sold a 600-ml bottle of cold drink for Rs 26 even though its MRP was Rs 25. The allegation concerned an overcharge of Re 1. The man was working at his wife's shop when the incident took place.

Meaning of repeating numbers: Angel signs and numerology explained
articles.summary: Repeating numbers such as 11:11 are often perceived as spiritual messages from the universe. They encourage individuals to take a moment to stop and contemplate their life paths. Each numeral imparts a unique significance, ranging from fresh starts to endings and personal evolution. While these numerical symbols provide insights, the onus of decision-making lies with the individual. Numerology enriches daily experiences, offering solace and direction that complement proactive choices.

articles.title: From Op Sindoor to Urgent Fury, how network warfare has changed the way conflicts are fought
articles.summary: Network-centric warfare is reshaping how wars are fought and won today. India faces significant security challenges across multiple domains simultaneously. Existing Indian defense networks like AFNET and DCN are crucial for integration. These systems enable faster battlefield decisions and shared operational pictures. Companies are actively developing capabilities for this evolving warfare.

In a dedicated four-hour effort, he and a team of volunteers successfully gathered an impressive 585 kilograms of litter. This endeavor was part of World Cleanup Day, supported by Philip Morris.

articles.title: TOI-DPA Airfare Index: A flight price tracker that will help you plan trips better
articles.summary: The TOI-DPA Airline Price Index monitors daily fluctuations in domestic airfares across India, illuminating trends in inflation, demand, and pricing strategies for various routes. Additionally, the Fare Timing Index reveals how ticket prices adjust over time related to booking. Factors such as departure times and specific days of the week play a critical role in determining fare costs, leading to valuable insights into airline pricing dynamics.

articles.title: 40-year-old man dies after Thar hits scooter in Greater Noida, wife injured

Neeraj succumbed to his injuries during treatment at a hospital. Police have taken the Thar SUV into custody and are searching for the driver. Legal proceedings are underway after obtaining a complaint from the victim's family.

articles.title: Delhi trekker found dead in 400m gorge in Ukhand’s Chopta while trying to take photo
articles.summary: A woman from Delhi tragically lost her life during a solo trip to Chopta when she slipped and fell into a deep gorge while trying to capture photographs. After her family reported her missing when she didn't return, rescue teams initiated a search operation that ultimately led to the discovery of her body. Authorities are currently investigating the circumstances surrounding this heartbreaking incident.

articles.title: Meet UP’s Green Army: Women fighting violence, addiction and child marriage
articles.summary: In Uttar Pradesh, women don green saris and wield lathis, forming the Green Army to tackle pressing village issues like gambling, alcohol misuse, and domestic violence. Drawing strength from their personal experiences, they advocate for girls' education and fight against child marriages. Their initiatives also include celebrating daughters' births and supporting sustainable livelihoods, fostering significant social transformation in rural areas.

articles.title: MakeMyTrip ordered to pay Rs 48,775 after two booked hotels found non-existent
articles.summary: A consumer commission ordered MakeMyTrip to refund Rs 18,775 for non-existent hotels. The complainant booked two properties which were not found at their listed locations. This led to the family sleeping in their car in sub-zero temperatures. MakeMyTrip was held liable for listing misrepresented and non-existent properties. The commission also awarded compensation and litigation costs to the aggrieved consumer.

Can you reshape a newborn’s nose with your fingers? Doctor debunks viral claim
articles.summary: A traditional practice suggests that pressing a baby's nose each day can help shape it more sharply over time. Nevertheless, doctors assert that this method does not effectively change the nose's structure. Unlike the skull, the cartilage in a nose remains pliable and does not possess internal rigidity. For a lasting change in nose shape, surgical procedures are necessary.

articles.title: How Puducherry offers housing sites to homeless and underprivileged communities
articles.summary: Puducherry is extending its generous initiative that provides free house plots to economically disadvantaged families and those belonging to scheduled caste communities. Since its inception in 1981, the scheme supports individuals who do not have land for housing. Eligible applicants must be Indian citizens with a yearly family income below Rs 24,000 and need to present a range of documents including identity, residence, income, and caste certificates.
